title: Committed 2MB app.bin build artifact in the PR tree (added by 0118cc0), unignored and platform-specific
evidence: git ls-files | grep -i '\.bin' → 'app.bin'; ls -la app.bin → '-rwxr-xr-x  1 moses  staff  2058072  9 Aug 15:47 app.bin'; git status --short after a local build → ' M app.bin'; .gitignore contains 'bin/' and 'goldens/_reports/' but no 'app.bin'
detail: The 2,058,072-byte macOS build artifact is tracked at the PR head with no .gitignore entry; a local rebuild dirties it (status 'M app.bin'), guaranteeing merge churn and platform-specific repo bloat.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached app.bin, add 'app.bin' to .gitignore, and let CI produce the binary.

title: The pair-index convention that shapes each pipe bezier is duplicated in 3 places; the 'one formula' anti-drift invariant covers only the control point
detail: The one-formula guarantee covers only the control point; the pair-index loop that actually shapes each curve is re-implemented in three places. A convention change or snapshot-vs-live ordering drift silently desyncs rendered pixels from the hit-test.
recommended_fix: Extract pair_idx computation into the shared pipe_control_point helper so both the render pass and nearest_pipe derive the curve from one source.

title: Per-run action log is heap-allocated and never freed — every run restart leaks the prior run's command log
evidence:
bus_submit: '	logged := cmd
	logged.apply_tick = apply_tick
	append(&rc.state.action_log, logged)
	resnapshot(rc) // the player sees the edit land instantly' (append uses the app's default context.allocator; step()'s 'context.allocator = state.allocator' is scoped to core.step only) and run_context_destroy: '	delete(rc.snapshot.nodes)
	delete(rc.snapshot.pipes)
	delete(rc.snapshot.packets)
	delete(rc.snapshot.classes)
	delete(rc.snapshot.forecasts)
	delete(rc.autopilot_wired)
	delete(rc.arena_buf)
	rc.state = nil' (no delete of action_log)
detail: bus_submit appends the log with the app's default heap allocator, and run_context_destroy never frees it — each R-key/win/lose restart leaks the prior run's log. Contradicts ODN-13/18's 'reset cannot leak state' claim.
recommended_fix: Route the action log through the run arena (state.allocator) or add delete(rc.state.action_log) in run_context_destroy.

title: App_Mode (the presentation FSM enum, ODN-13) is defined in the sim core package, which never references it
evidence: core/types.odin:56: 'App_Mode :: enum u8 { Boot, Menu, Run, Paused, Game_Over }'; autopilot.odin:10: 'App_Mode :: pp.App_Mode'; main.odin:18: 'mode:       prun.App_Mode,'
detail: ODN-13 places the mode FSM in the app layer; the pure sim core defines the presentation-only Boot/Menu/Run/Paused/Game_Over states. The core now knows app states it never uses — a small boundary inversion.
recommended_fix: Move App_Mode to app/run or app/ and drop the core/types.odin definition.

title: TICK_SECONDS :: 0.1 hardcoded literal claims catalog derivation but is unused and silently contradicts balance.json if logic_hz changes
evidence: app/run/run.odin:11: 'TICK_SECONDS :: 0.1 // derived from balance.logic_hz at boot (catalog is the single source)'; grep shows the only reference is the definition itself; the real value is 'rc.driver.tick_seconds = 1.0 / f64(catalogs.balance.logic_hz)' in run_context_create
detail: The constant is dead (the driver uses tick_seconds from the catalog) yet claims catalog derivation. If logic_hz is retuned, this literal silently lies — the Godot ms_per_tick lesson fossilized as misleading dead code.
recommended_fix: Delete TICK_SECONDS, or compute it from catalogs.balance.logic_hz at boot and reference it.

title: core/testkit.odin declares 'NOT used by the game' but the shipped game's A-key autopilot calls testkit_wire_boot/testkit_autowire
detail: The harness-only boundary is fictional: the game executable ships core testkit code behind the autopilot key. The behavior is sound (commands log with apply_tick and replay), but the documented boundary claim is false.
recommended_fix: Move the autopilot wiring procs into a run-layer helper, or amend the testkit header to state the game autopilot consumes them.

title: Grace countdown pip computes secs then discards it (_ = secs) and renders a literal '!' — the countdown numeral never appears
evidence:
'// grace countdown pip
	if snap.in_grace {
		buf: [32]u8
		secs := snap.grace_ticks_left * i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
		_ = secs
		txt := fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "!", 0)
		draw_text(v, txt, {x + w + 8, y}, 18, p.state_critical)
	}'
detail: The pip computes the countdown seconds then discards them, rendering a static '!'. Dead computation misleads future editors into thinking a countdown is shown; the value is never formatted into the buffer.
recommended_fix: Render the actual seconds via fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "%d", secs) or delete the dead computation and keep the '!' as a deliberate pip.
